question: What is the purpose of the Nmfaf_3daDataManagement_Deconfigure service operation? [3GPP Release 18]
options: To configure the MFAF to map data or analytics received by the MFAF to out-bound notification endpoints
To configure the MFAF to stop mapping data or analytics received by the MFAF to out-bound notification endpoints
To supply data or analytics from the MFAF to notification endpoints
To fetch data or analytics from the MFAF based on fetch instructions
explanation: The Nmfaf_3daDataManagement_Deconfigure service operation is used to stop mapping data or analytics received by the MFAF to one or more out-bound notification endpoints.

question: When are devices required to send the GTS Request command? [IEEE 802.15.4]
options: Only devices without a short address
Only devices capable of sending it
explanation: All devices that have been assigned a short address shall send the GTS Request command.

question: How does a supporting UE attach to the same core network operator from which it detached in a shared network? [3GPP Release 17]
options: It requests the core network node to remember its previous selection.
It uses information stored in the UE when it was detached.
It relies on the SIM/USIM card for information.
It performs a fresh attach procedure.
explanation: A supporting UE in a shared network attaches to the same core network operator it detached from by using information stored in the UE when it was detached.

question: When can the setting of the Privacy exception list be changed? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The setting of the Privacy exception list can be changed anytime.

question: What does the NEF notify to the AF after determining the suitable DNAI(s)? [3GPP Release 18]
options: DNAI(s) or the updated DNAI information
explanation: After determining the suitable DNAI(s), NEF notifies the DNAI(s) or the updated DNAI information to AF.

question: In online charging, how are chargeable events transformed into charging events? [3GPP Release 18]
explanation: The CTF transforms each chargeable event into a charging event and forwards these charging events to the OCF in real-time.

question: What is the purpose of the PSFCH channel in NR V2X sidelink? [3GPP Release 16]
options: To transmit Uplink and Downlink V2X messages
To transmit HARQ feedback for unicast and groupcast
To transmit physical layer structure information
explanation: The PSFCH channel in NR V2X sidelink is used to transmit sidelink HARQ feedback for unicast and groupcast services. It provides feedback on the success or failure of the whole transport block and triggers for channel state information (CSI) feedback.

question: What is the spreading ratio in a direct-sequence system? [IEEE 802.11]
options: The power level of the transmitted signal
The number of chips used to transmit a single bit
The data rate of the transmission
The size of the frequency band
The correlation function of the receiver
explanation: The spreading ratio is the number of chips used to transmit a single bit in a direct-sequence system.

question: Why does an originator regularly send a BlockAckReq frame in the GCR Block Ack retransmission policy? [IEEE 802.11]
options: To indicate the end of the transmission
To request acknowledgment from the group members
To minimize buffering latency at the receivers
explanation: Regularly sending a BlockAckReq frame with the GCR Group Address subfield set to the GCR group address and the Block Ack Starting Sequence Control subfield set to the earliest A-MSDU minimizes buffering latency at receivers in the GCR group.

question: Which feature proposes to integrate selected WLAN direct discovery technologies as an alternative technology for ProSe Direct Discovery? [3GPP Release 15]
options: Enhancements to LTE operation in unlicensed spectrum
explanation: The feature that proposes to integrate selected WLAN direct discovery technologies as an alternative technology for ProSe Direct Discovery is the WLAN Offloading System.

question: What is the maximum number of S-NSIs that a GN-NSI can consist of?
explanation: A GN-NSI can consist of up to eight S-NSIs in the Sub Network Slicing architecture.

question: When can there be two N3 tunnel terminations at the RAN for a PDU Session? [3GPP Release 18]
options: When there are multiple PDU Session Ids for the PDU Session
When the QoS Flows of the PDU Session are split across the two RATs
When the PDU Session belongs to a specific Network Slice
When the Master RAN node is congested
When the Secondary RAN node is congested
explanation: If the DL User Plane traffic of some QoS Flows of a PDU Session are directed to the Secondary RAN Node while the remaining QoS Flows are directed to the Master RAN Node, there will be two N3 tunnel terminations at the RAN for such PDU Session.

question: What is the main benefit of the platooning use case in NR-V2X?
options: Enhanced perception, planning, and control in road users
explanation: The platooning use case in NR-V2X enables vehicles to follow each other closely with a reduced safety distance, resulting in increased traffic efficiency.

question: Which NGAP procedure is used for inter-system load balancing? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The NGAP procedure used for inter-system load balancing is Uplink RAN Configuration Transfer.

question: What is the purpose of the Validity Period for predictions? [3GPP Release 18]
options: To indicate the area of interest
To provide the Target of Analytics Reporting
To specify the maximum number of objects
explanation: The Validity Period for predictions is used to define the time window for which the predictions are valid.

question: What is the purpose of the MCImp-MC_ARCH work item? [3GPP Release 14]
options: To specify a common functional architecture for MCVideo
To specify a common functional architecture for MCData
To specify a common functional architecture for all mission critical services
To specify a common functional architecture for MCPTT only
explanation: The main objective of the MCImp-MC_ARCH work item is to specify a common functional architecture for all mission critical services.

question: What are the most harmful RF exposure hazards? [IEEE C95.1]
explanation: RF shocks and burns constitute the most harmful RF exposure hazard.

question: What should the UE consider if it cannot detect any cell meeting the S criterion on a frequency for sidelink operation? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Out-of-coverage for sidelink operation on that frequency
Out-of-coverage for V2X sidelink communication on that frequency
Out-of-coverage for NR sidelink communication on that frequency
In-coverage for NR sidelink communication on that frequency
In-coverage for sidelink operation on that frequency
explanation: If the UE cannot detect any cell on a frequency meeting the S criterion, it shall consider itself to be out-of-coverage for sidelink operation on that frequency.

question: What is the purpose of the Member UE selection assistance functionality hosted by NEF? [3GPP Release 18]
options: To provide filtering criteria for AF's inputs
To collect corresponding data from relevant 5GC NFs
To select member UEs for AF's application operations
To provide QoS for the updated list of UEs
To assist the AI/ML application server in scheduling UEs
explanation: The Member UE selection assistance functionality hosted by NEF is used to assist the AF in selecting member UEs that can be used in application operations such as AI/ML based applications.

question: What happens when a mobile station issues a successful association request in 802.11 wireless networks? [IEEE 802.11]
options: The access point responds with a status code of 0 and the AID
The access point responds with a deauthentication frame
The access point buffers frames for the mobile station in a power-saving state
The access point bridges frames from Ethernet to the wireless medium
The access point initiates the reassociation procedure
explanation: When a successful association request is issued, the access point responds with a status code of 0 (successful) and the Association ID (AID).

question: When does the AMF enable or disable the 5G access stratum time distribution for a UE? [3GPP Release 18]
options: When UE is in CM-REJECTED state
When UE is in CM-IDLE state
When UE is in CM-REGISTERED state
When UE is in CM-DISCONNECTED state
When UE is in CM-CONNECTED state
explanation: If the AMF receives start and stop times, it sends a message to the NG-RAN to enable or disable the 5G access stratum time distribution according to the expiry of start and stop times when the UE is in CM-CONNECTED state.

question: When can target UEs be positioned for lawful interception services? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Only if the target UE user authorizes it
Only if the privacy attribute value allows positioning
Under all circumstances required by local regulatory requirements
explanation: Target UEs can be positioned for lawful interception services under all circumstances required by local regulatory requirements.

question: What is an advantage of lower frequency (sub-GHz) imaging compared to mmWave/THz imaging?
options: Lower frequency is less impacted by interference
Lower frequency has shorter exposure time
explanation: Lower frequency (sub-GHz) imaging has wider coverage compared to mmWave/THz imaging.

question: What is the purpose of data frames in 802.11? [IEEE 802.11]
options: To carry data from station to station
To perform area clearing and carrier-sensing maintenance
To join and leave wireless networks
To indicate whether frames are buffered for a station
explanation: Data frames in 802.11 are used to haul data from station to station.

question: What are DCI formats with CRC scrambled by MCCH-RNTI or G-RNTI referred to as? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: DCI formats with CRC scrambled by MCCH-RNTI or G-RNTI for broadcast scheduling PDSCH receptions are referred to as broadcast DCI formats.

question: When can the unused portion of a polled TXOP be reallocated by the HC? [IEEE 802.11]
options: When a PHY-CCA.indication (BUSY) primitive occurs at the STA expecting the Ack frame
When the expected Ack frame is not received
When there is not enough time to transmit a QoS Null frame
When the STA ceases control of the channel
When there are no frames to be sent to the HC
explanation: The unused portion of a polled TXOP can be reallocated by the HC when there are no frames to be sent to the HC.

question: What are the two different architectures specified by MulteFire for deployment?
options: Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) access mode and Neutral Host Network (NHN) access mode
explanation: MulteFire specifies two different architectures for deployment: Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) access mode and Neutral Host Network (NHN) access mode.

question: What UL (uplink) transmission scheme does MulteFire use?
explanation: MulteFire uses Block Interleaved FDMA (B-IFDMA) as the UL transmission scheme.

question: What is the key difference between Digital Twin-based systems and existing network simulation and planning tools?
options: Digital Twin-based systems are not connected to deployed physical subsystems
Digital Twin-based systems do not evolve as the deployment proceeds
Digital Twin-based systems are connected to deployed physical subsystems and the whole system evolves as the deployment proceeds
Digital Twin-based systems do not use Artificial Intelligence
explanation: The document states that the key difference in Digital Twin-based systems compared to existing network simulation and planning tools is that they are connected to deployed physical subsystems and the whole system evolves as the deployment proceeds.

question: What kind of access can enterprise UEs have to non-public networks? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Access to the non-public network of the enterprise only
Access to both a non-public network and a PLMN
Access to a PLMN and a non-public network via a different network
Access to a PLMN and a non-public network via multiple subscriptions
explanation: Some enterprise UEs can be restricted to only access the non-public network of the enterprise, while others can access both a non-public network and a PLMN where specifically allowed.

question: What is the purpose of the TRP Measurement Grid? [3GPP Release 18]
options: To calculate the CDF of the EIRP/EIS distribution in 3D
To determine the total power radiated by the DUT in the TX beam peak direction
To determine the TX and RX beam peak direction
To perform TRP measurements taken on the sampling grid
To perform 3D Throughput/RSRP/EIS scans for RX beam peak direction
explanation: The TRP Measurement Grid is used to perform TRP measurements taken on the sampling grid to determine the total power radiated by the DUT in the TX beam peak direction.

question: What action is necessary to get access to services in Idle mode? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: Camping on a cell is necessary to get access to services in Idle mode.

question: How does EC-GSM-IoT improve coverage performance for Cellular IoT devices? [3GPP Release 14]
options: By using modified channel coding schemes
explanation: EC-GSM-IoT improves the coverage performance of Cellular IoT devices by using modified channel coding schemes.

question: What triggers the NF/NF Service Context Transfer Push procedure? [3GPP Release 18]
options: The Target NF/NF Service receiving a notification about the decommissioning
The Source NF informing the NRF about the decommissioning
The Source NF sending a request to the Target NF/NF Service
The Target NF/NF Service receiving a request from the Source NF/NF Service
The Target NF/NF Service setting up necessary information about the new context location
explanation: When triggered, the Source NF/NF Service acting as an NF Service Consumer sends its Context to the Target NF/NF Service acting as an NF Service Producer by sending a request.

question: Which 5G vertical domain is the maritime domain a part of? [3GPP Release 16]
explanation: The maritime domain is one of the 5G vertical domains in 3GPP.

question: What is the maximum power spectrum density (PSD) allowed in the 5350-5470 MHz range in Europe?
explanation: The maximum power spectrum density (PSD) allowed in the 5350-5470 MHz range in Europe is 17 dBm/MHz.

question: Which technology was introduced in 3G systems to improve video and audio streaming capabilities?
explanation: Wideband Code Division Multiple Access (W-CDMA) was introduced in 3G systems to improve video and audio streaming capabilities.

question: What does GFSK stand for in the context of frequency shift keying? [IEEE 802.11]
explanation: GFSK stands for Gaussian Frequency Shift Keying in the context of frequency shift keying.

question: What is the purpose of the User Configuration mechanism in the IMS Multimedia Telephony service? [3GPP Release 17]
options: To support synchronization of communication logs between multiple devices
To indicate which identities are active or inactive on a specific UE
To provide user preferences for media handling capabilities
To modify the Caller Identity Analytics function
explanation: The User Configuration mechanism allows an authorized user to indicate which identities are active or inactive on a specific UE.

question: What is the purpose of packet buffering in Edge Relocation? [3GPP Release 18]
options: To prevent packet loss during EAS migration
To enable simultaneous connectivity over source and target PSA
To eliminate the need for EAS IP replacement
explanation: Packet buffering is used in Edge Relocation to buffer uplink packets and prevent packet loss when the application client sends UL packets to a new EAS before it is ready to handle them.

question: What does the Multi-Identity (MiD) service enable? [3GPP Release 16]
options: A user to use different UEs registered under different public user identities
A user to use different identities on a single UE
Call distribution to different members of a group or firm
A user to share identities with another user
A user to use different UEs that are registered under the same public user identity
explanation: The Multi-Identity (MiD) service enables a user to use different identities on a single UE.

question: What can be adjusted to ensure responses from all access points in an area can be processed during active scanning? [IEEE 802.11]
explanation: The maximum channel time can be adjusted to ensure responses from all access points in an area can be processed during active scanning.

question: What is the maximum number of PDU Sessions? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The maximum number of PDU Sessions is 256.

question: Which identity is used for indication of pre-emption in the downlink? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: INT-RNTI is used for indication of pre-emption in the downlink.

question: What is the role of the Master-SCS/AS in the Sub Network Slicing architecture?
options: To request the GN-NSI from the operator.
To manage and control the Slave-SCS/ASs.
To allocate resources and control S-NSIs.
To grant or deny the GN-NSI's request.
To define the attributes and design the NST of GN-NSI.
explanation: The role of the Master-SCS/AS is to manage and control the Slave-SCS/ASs in the Sub Network Slicing architecture.

question: Which entity controls the packet duplication functionality in DC (dual connectivity)?
explanation: The packet duplication functionality in DC is controlled by the MgNB, which is responsible for transmitting the same PDCP PDU via the MgNB and the SgNB.

question: What is the purpose of the group identifier called 'External Group ID'? [3GPP Release 14]
options: To identify individual UEs within a group
To resolve the group ID to individual UE ID
To reduce signalling for sending event reports of group members
To indicate the time for which monitoring event reporting can be aggregated
To handle group-based enhancements in the network capability exposure function
explanation: The group identifier 'External Group ID' is used to identify the group of UEs and is resolved to individual UE ID by the HSS or PCRF.

question: When can the V-SMF delete the DNS context from the selected V-EASDF? [3GPP Release 18]
options: When the request for HR-SBO is not authorized
When the V-SMF selects a new V-EASDF
When the UE initiates a Mobility Registration Update procedure
When the AF triggers EAS rediscovery
explanation: If the request for HR-SBO is not authorized and a DNS context had been created, the V-SMF deletes the DNS context from the selected V-EASDF.

question: What does a UE determine when selecting a power for an S-SS/PSBCH block transmission occasion? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Number of resource blocks for a S-SS/PSBCH block transmission
Value of dl-P0-PSBCH-r16 if provided, else dl-Alpha-PSBCH
explanation: A UE determines a power for an S-SS/PSBCH block transmission occasion based on the value of dl-P0-PSBCH-r16 if provided, else dl-Alpha-PSBCH.

question: According to the norm, what is the maximum power that a PD can use in Ethernet? [IEEE 802.3]
explanation: The norm specifies that a PD cannot use more than 12.95W of power.

question: What is supported in enhanced TTI bundling compared to Rel-13 CE mode A in eMTC? [3GPP Release 14]
options: Different repetition levels of scheduled PUSCH
explanation: Enhanced TTI bundling supports additional repetition numbers, including 12 and 24, compared to Rel-13 CE mode A in eMTC.

question: What is the purpose of the MasterInformationBlockSidelink message? [3GPP Release 17]
options: To indicate the failure of a PC5 RRC AS reconfiguration
To transfer UE radio access capabilities
To include sidelink DRX assistance information used to determine the sidelink DRX configuration
To include the system information transmitted by a UE via SL-BCH
explanation: The purpose of the MasterInformationBlockSidelink message is to include the system information transmitted by a UE via SL-BCH.

question: What is the indication used to invoke the terminal application in the peer end of a multimedia call? [3GPP Release 18]
explanation: In the peer end of a multimedia call, the H.324 information is used to invoke the terminal application.

question: What is the role of the bearer control function? [3GPP Release 18]
options: To provide interfaces for supplementary services
To define the characteristics of bearers
To assign and release bearers for a call
To enable subscribers to control services
To adapt bearers for fixed network use
explanation: The bearer control function is responsible for the assignment and release of bearers for a call.

question: What is the purpose of interworking between a 5G core network and an EPC? [3GPP Release 17]
options: To support home network provided data connectivity
To preserve IP address for PS service
To provide support for services in the home network
To support mobility procedures with minimum impact to the user experience
explanation: The 5G system shall support mobility procedures between a 5G core network and an EPC with minimum impact to the user experience.

question: What does the Relaxed monitoring for cell reselection feature in NB-IoT allow the UE to do? [3GPP Release 15]
options: Avoid monitoring neighbouring cells for 24 hours in stationary or non-changing network topology
Request NPUSCH resources for BSR transmission
Reduce system acquisition time for the UE
Support small cell deployments with lower maximum transmit power
Improve the accuracy of narrowband measurement
explanation: The Relaxed monitoring for cell reselection feature allows the UE to avoid monitoring neighbouring cells for 24 hours in cases where the UE is stationary and/or the network topology is not changing. This helps to extend UE battery life.

question: What is the purpose of the Radio Network Information Service (RNIS) offered by MEC (Multi-access Edge Computing)?
options: To provide actual RAN information relating to the User Equipments (UEs) in the network
To estimate the location of vehicles and pedestrians
To trigger user-specific traffic rules on the MEC platform
To reserve networking resources at the host
To provide predictions on the Quality-of-Service (QoS) performance of the V2I link
explanation: The Radio Network Information Service (RNIS) provides actual RAN information relating to the User Equipments (UEs) in the network.

question: What was the spatial peak SAR value set at in ANSI C95.1-1982? [IEEE C95.1]
explanation: The spatial peak SAR in ANSI C95.1-1982 was set at 8 W/kg.

question: What happens during session termination in online charging? [3GPP Release 18]
options: The resource usage is debited from the subscriber account immediately
The network element sends an interim charging event
A certain amount of units is blocked on the subscriber's account
The CDF produces a matching CDR
The value of unused quota is returned to the subscriber's account
explanation: During session termination in online charging, the value of any unused quota is returned by the network element to the OCS/CCS, which then returns it to the subscriber's account.

question: What is the purpose of the Header Checksum in the IP header? [TCP/IP]
options: To represent the length of the header
To check if the IP header is valid
To calculate the total length of the IP packet
explanation: The Header Checksum is a check value used to validate the IP header.

question: What is the purpose of spread spectrum technology in unlicensed devices? [IEEE 802.11]
options: To increase the transmitted power of the devices
To diffuse signal power over a large range of frequencies
To restrict the use of radio signals in certain areas
To encode the transmitted data for security purposes
explanation: Spread spectrum technology is used in unlicensed devices to diffuse signal power over a large range of frequencies, making transmissions look like noise to narrowband receivers.

question: How does an AP set up the protection for the duration of the sectorized beam transmission in an SO frame exchange sequence? [IEEE 802.11]
options: By transmitting an ACK or Response frame after the omnidirectional beam transmission.
By setting the NAV for the duration of the sectorized beam transmission.
By transmitting a BF duration frame after the omnidirectional beam transmission.
By switching to the sectorized beam transmission after the omnidirectional preamble.
By transmitting a NAV protected frame after the omnidirectional beam transmission.
explanation: In an SO frame exchange sequence, the AP sets up the protection for the duration of the sectorized beam transmission by switching to the sectorized beam transmission after the omnidirectional preamble of the long preamble.

question: Can any party in a multiparty call undergo voice call continuity? [3GPP Release 18]
options: Yes, any party in a multiparty call can undergo voice call continuity
No, only the calling party can undergo voice call continuity
No, only the called party can undergo voice call continuity
No, voice call continuity is not supported for multiparty calls
explanation: It is possible for any party in a multiparty call to undergo voice call continuity and stay in the call. The entire multiparty call can be terminated when the served mobile subscriber releases, even if they are connected via IMS.

question: How does packet duplication potentially reduce jitter?
options: By providing frequency and path diversity
By improving throughput during TCP slow start phase
explanation: Packet duplication potentially reduces jitter by minimizing the variance in latency.

question: What is covered by enhanced application layer support for V2X services? [3GPP Release 17]
options: V2X communication over NR PC5 reference point
explanation: Enhanced application layer support for V2X services covers the support of advanced V2X services, considering existing stage 1 and stage 2 work within 3GPP and V2X application requirements defined outside 3GPP.

question: What does the Omni field indicate? [IEEE 802.11]
options: The Omni field indicates the type of sectorization operation.
The Omni field indicates if the present transmission is sectorized or omnidirectional.
The Omni field indicates the duration of the current sector transmissions.
The Omni field indicates the ID of the active sector.
The Omni field is reserved when sectorization is activated.
explanation: The Omni field indicates if the present transmission is sectorized or omnidirectional.

question: What is the purpose of the UE Capability Management Function (UCMF)? [3GPP Release 16]
options: To store UE radio capability IDs
To assign UE radio capability IDs
To provision UE radio capability IDs
explanation: The UE Capability Management Function (UCMF) is used to store, assign, and provision UE radio capability IDs.

question: How does a non-supporting UE select a core network operator to serve it in a shared network? [3GPP Release 17]
options: The UE selects an operator from the available CN operators.
The shared network selects an operator for the UE.
The RAN routes the UE to an available CN node.
The BSC/RNC/eNodeB relays the chosen operator to the core network node.
explanation: A non-supporting UE in a shared network has the operator selected by the shared network.

question: For PSFCH transmission with HARQ-ACK information, how are the PRBs allocated? [3GPP Release 17]
options: In an ascending order of the PRB index only
In an ascending order of the cyclic shift pair index only
In an ascending order of both the PRB index and the cyclic shift pair index
explanation: For PSFCH transmission with HARQ-ACK information, the PRBs are allocated in an ascending order of both the PRB index and the cyclic shift pair index.

question: What determines the energy detection threshold in channel access procedures? [3GPP Release 17]
options: The maximum eNB/gNB output power in dBm for the channel
The single channel bandwidth in MHz
The absence of any other technology sharing the channel
explanation: The energy detection threshold in channel access procedures is determined by the maximum eNB/gNB output power, single channel bandwidth, and the absence of any other technology sharing the channel.

question: What does the Load-Balancing steering mode do? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Splits the traffic of a data flow across 3GPP and non-3GPP accesses
Balances the load on the core network nodes
Restricts the UE to a single access type
explanation: The Load-Balancing steering mode splits the traffic of a data flow across 3GPP and non-3GPP accesses in both uplink and downlink directions separately.

question: What is the length of the source MAC address field in an Ethernet frame? [IEEE 802.3]
explanation: The source MAC address field in an Ethernet frame is 6 bytes long.

question: What does the home environment need to provide to the visited network when allowing a subscriber to roam to different domains? [3GPP Release 18]
explanation: The document states that when an operator allows a subscriber to roam to different domains, the home environment needs to provide subscription data to the visited network.

question: What does VarConnEstFailReportList include? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: VarConnEstFailReportList includes a list of the connection establishment failure and/or connection resume failure information.

question: What is the definition of the Chip Rate field value '1'? [IEEE 802.15.4]
explanation: The Chip Rate field value '1' corresponds to 600 kchip/s.

question: Which interface is used to transfer short messages between the SGSN and SMS-GMSC/SMS-IWMSC? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The Gd-interface is used to transfer short messages between the SGSN and SMS-GMSC/SMS-IWMSC.

question: What does the RRC protocol offer to upper layers? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Transfer of application layer measurement configuration and reporting
explanation: The RRC protocol offers the service of broadcasting common control information to upper layers.

question: What is SIPTO at the Local Network? [3GPP Release 17]
options: A collocated L-GW in the eNB
A collocated S-GW and L-GW in the eNB
explanation: SIPTO at the Local Network refers to the use of a collocated L-GW in the eNB or a standalone GW to support certain functions.

question: In the indirect communication model without delegated discovery, what is the role of the SCP? [3GPP Release 18]
options: It authorizes the NF service consumer's request
It selects the NF service producer instance for the NF service consumer
It stores and marks the NF service consumer as available
It routes the request from the NF service consumer to the selected NF service producer instance
It notifies the NF service consumer of newly registered/updated/deregistered NF instances
explanation: In the indirect communication model without delegated discovery, the SCP routes the request from the NF service consumer to the selected NF service producer instance.

question: What does MulteFire rely on for providing service to users?
explanation: MulteFire relies only on the unlicensed spectrum for providing service to users.

question: Have low levels of RF exposure been shown to cause changes in hormones in laboratory animals? [IEEE C95.1]
options: Yes, there are consistent changes in hormones
Yes, but the changes are inconsistent
No, there are no changes in hormones
There is not enough evidence to determine
explanation: A handful of reports cite changes in melatonin and various other hormones in laboratory animals after low levels of RF exposure, although most hormone changes observed in animals have been at clearly thermal RF exposure levels. In some cases, it is difficult to determine whether exposure levels were thermal or not, and small sample size is frequently a problem.

question: When is Paging with Wake Up Signal (WUS) used? [3GPP Release 17]
options: When the UE is in RRC_INACTIVE state
When the UE is in RRC_IDLE state
When the UE detects a PTW
explanation: Paging with Wake Up Signal (WUS) is used in the RRC_IDLE state when the UE detects WUS and needs to monitor the following POs or receive a paging message.

question: What is the purpose of CIDR addressing? [TCP/IP]
explanation: CIDR addressing is used to restructure IP addresses, simplify global routing tables, and enable route aggregation as mentioned in the content.

question: In unpaired spectrum operation, when are a DL BWP and an UL BWP linked together? [3GPP Release 17]
options: When the DL BWP index and the UL BWP index are the same
When the center frequency for both BWP is the same
When they have the same SCS configuration
When they have the same number of RB sets
explanation: In unpaired spectrum operation, a DL BWP and an UL BWP are linked together when the DL BWP index and the UL BWP index are the same.

question: Which version of SNMP provides authentication and privacy? [TCP/IP]
explanation: SNMPv3 provides authentication and privacy in addition to the features of SNMPv2.

question: In which scenario are Hybrid Access Networks primarily deployed?
options: Urban areas with high-speed xDSL connections
Rural areas with limited xDSL connectivity
Data centers with high bandwidth requirements
Enterprise networks with multiple Internet connections
Public Wi-Fi networks with high user density
explanation: Hybrid Access Networks are primarily deployed in rural areas where the length of the twisted pair lines does not allow the xDSL technologies to reach high speeds.

question: How is Extended Access Barring supported in shared networks? [3GPP Release 17]
options: The BSC/RNC/eNodeB configures the UE for access barring.
The shared network applies access barring uniformly for all UEs.
The UE requests access barring for specific operators.
The BSC/RNC/eNodeB provides independent support for each sharing operator.
explanation: In shared networks, the BSC/RNC/eNodeB provides independent support for the barring of MSs configured for Extended Access Barring for each sharing operator.

question: What are the peak packet data rates supported by the Evolved Packet System on the radio access bearer? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The radio access network of the Evolved Packet System is capable of supporting instantaneous peak packet data rates of 100 Mbps on the radio access bearer downlink to the UE and 50 Mbps on the uplink.

question: What can be queried from the management information base (MIB) in the 802.11 protocol? [IEEE 802.11]
explanation: The 802.11 MIB contains objects that can be queried to gain status information about the network interface.

question: What is a Personal IoT Network (PIN)? [3GPP Release 17]
options: A network located within a residence, office or shop that provides connectivity to the 5G network.
A network owned, installed, and configured by a public network operator.
A network that consists of PIN Elements and communicates using PIN Direct Connection.
A network that supports mechanisms for identifying a PIN, PIN Element, eRG, and PRAS.
A network that supports regulatory requirements for emergency calls, PWS, and eCall for UEs connected via 3GPP access.
explanation: A Personal IoT Network (PIN) is described as a network that consists of PIN Elements that communicate using PIN Direct Connection or direct network connection and is managed locally.

question: What criteria are considered for network broadcast geographic area coverage management? [3GPP Release 18]
options: OTT provider request and available network capacity
OTT provider request and number of users under broadcast network coverage
Location information of UE and number of users under broadcast network coverage
OTT provider request and location information of UE
Number of users under broadcast network coverage and available network capacity
explanation: According to the document, network broadcast geographic area coverage management considers OTT provider request (including the potential coverage information of TV service information) and the number of users under broadcast network coverage.

question: What does the 5G system need to provide for mobile base station relays using 5G connectivity provided by a different MNO? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Separate network infrastructure for MNO-B to communicate with MNO-A through the relay
Specific QoS handling for traffic relayed through the MNO-B's network
Ability for MNO-A and MNO-B to share relay resources for UEs connected to the 5G network
Authorization from MNO-A for MNO-B to provide 5G connectivity through the relay
Ownership and control of the relay by MNO-A despite using connectivity from MNO-B
explanation: The 5G system needs to support RAN sharing between multiple PLMNs for UEs connected to the 5G network via mobile base station relays, assuming that relay and (donor) RAN resources are shared among operators.

question: When can a UE apply Type 1 channel access procedures for a UL transmission(s)? [3GPP Release 17]
options: After performing Type 2 channel access procedures
explanation: A UE can apply Type 1 channel access procedures for a UL transmission(s) after receiving the corresponding capability.

question: Which power saving scheme achieves power consumption reduction by potentially skipping PDCCH monitoring at subsequent slots of PDSCH/PUSCH transmission? [3GPP Release 16]
explanation: The power saving scheme of multi-slot scheduling achieves power consumption reduction by potentially skipping PDCCH monitoring at subsequent slots of PDSCH/PUSCH transmission.

question: What type of authentication and authorization is required for accessing a 5G VN group? [3GPP Release 18]
explanation: Accessing a 5G VN group requires secondary authentication and authorization, which is performed as part of the PDU Session Establishment procedure.

question: What does the timing advance command for a TAG indicate? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Change of synchronization signal transmission timing
Change of downlink timing relative to the current downlink timing
Change of uplink timing relative to the current uplink timing
Change of broadcast channel transmission timing
explanation: The timing advance command for a TAG indicates the change of uplink timing relative to the current uplink timing.

question: What does the SFD (Start Frame Delimiter) field in the PLCP framing indicate? [IEEE 802.11]
options: The synchronization between the transmitter and receiver
The power level of the signal
The frequency of the incoming signal
The type of modulation scheme used
explanation: The SFD field in the PLCP framing marks the end of the preamble and the beginning of the frame.

question: What can be configured separately for each SPS configuration in LTE? [3GPP Release 18]
options: The cyclic shift for the UL Demodulation Reference Signal (DMRS)
explanation: In LTE, the cyclic shift for the UL Demodulation Reference Signal (DMRS) can be configured independently for each SPS configuration.

question: What is the data rate for each clock pulse in 100Base-T? [IEEE 802.3]
explanation: For the 10Base-T standard, every data bit is coded in one physical bit. So, 1 bit is sent for every clock pulse.

question: What are the supported scenarios for MPS for MMTEL voice? [3GPP Release 18]
options: MPS for MMTEL voice and voice conference calls for an authorized Service User using a UE with an MPS subscription
MPS for MMTEL voice and voice conference calls for an authorized Service User using a UE that does not have an MPS subscription
MPS for all participants of an authorized MMTEL voice conference call
explanation: The system shall support MPS for MMTEL voice and voice conference calls for an authorized Service User using a UE with an MPS subscription, a UE that does not have an MPS subscription, and all participants of an authorized MMTEL voice conference call.

question: What channel carries the MulteFire system information broadcast (SIB-MulteFire)?
explanation: The MulteFire system information broadcast (SIB-MulteFire) is transmitted through the Physical Downlink Shared Channel (PDSCH) and carries information similar to the SIB1 and SIB2 messages of LTE Rel-13.

question: What is the high quality criterion for reporting a PLMN to the NAS in the E-UTRA and NB-IoT case? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Measured RSRP value greater than or equal to -110 dBm
Measured RSRP value less than -110 dBm
Measured RSRP value greater than or equal to -100 dBm
Measured RSRP value less than -100 dBm
Measured RSRP value greater than or equal to -120 dBm
explanation: The high quality criterion for reporting a PLMN to the NAS in the E-UTRA and NB-IoT case is a measured RSRP value greater than or equal to -110 dBm.

question: What power saving gain range is observed for the power saving scheme with UE adaptation to the number of antenna/MIMO layer? [3GPP Release 16]
explanation: The power saving gain for the power saving scheme with UE adaptation to the number of antenna/MIMO layer ranges from 6% to 30%.

question: What does the SIP Reason header extension work item do? [3GPP Release 14]
options: Specifies procedures for interworking of eCall over IMS to CS domain
Introduces password protection for activation of supplementary services in IMS
Ensures consistency of all the possible extensions of the SIP Reason header field
Provides media handling extensions for IMS-based telepresence
explanation: The SIP Reason header extension work item ensures consistency of all the possible extensions of the SIP Reason header field.

question: What is the main objective of intent driven management for service or network management? [3GPP Release 17]
options: To support monitoring of the progress of file download in a downloading job
To provide detailed knowledge of the underlying network resources
To optimize the provisioning of management services for UEs in a specified area
To reduce the complexity of management for network resources
To enhance the support for the NSA in the service-based management architecture
explanation: The intent driven management aims to reduce the complexity of management without getting into the intricate detail of the underlying network resources.

question: What is the RRC buffer size for a UE? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The RRC buffer size for a UE is 45 Kbytes.

question: What is the definition of the open-circuit voltage? [IEEE C95.1]
options: The potential difference between two conducting objects with a current load being applied
The potential difference between two conducting objects without a current load being applied
The current flowing through an open circuit
The resistance of an open circuit
The power dissipated in an open circuit
explanation: The open-circuit voltage is the potential difference between two conducting objects without a current load being applied to the objects.

question: What does the ECS provide to the EEC? [3GPP Release 18]
explanation: The ECS provides Edge configuration information to the EEC.

question: What is the purpose of the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI)? [ETSI NFV Release 5]
explanation: The purpose of the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) is firmware interface standardization.

question: Which of the following is NOT a possible status for a TCP socket? [TCP/IP]
explanation: Connected is not a valid status for a TCP socket.

question: Are the MuD and MiD services mutually exclusive? [3GPP Release 16]
options: Yes, a user can only use either MuD or MiD service at a time
No, they can both be used at the same time
No, a user can switch between MuD and MiD services
Yes, a user can only use MuD service on one type of UE and MiD service on another
No, a user can only use either MuD or MiD service based on their subscription

question: What does the Window field in the TCP header indicate? [TCP/IP]
options: The expected sequence number from the partner
The length of the TCP header in 32-bit words
The maximum number of data bytes that can be sent before a confirmation is sent
The check value of the TCP packet
explanation: The Window field in the TCP header indicates the maximum number of data bytes that can be sent before a confirmation is sent and received.

question: What is the main drawback of using proprietary approaches for stronger security in WEP? [IEEE 802.11]
options: Weakness in the key scheduling algorithm
Lack of interoperability on multivendor networks
explanation: Proprietary approaches for stronger security in WEP are a single-vendor solution and do not guarantee interoperability on multivendor networks.

question: What does the feature 'Accessing a list of deferred data communications' enable for the MCData service? [3GPP Release 15]
options: Sharing the current MCData system defined status
Real-time updates of changes to group dynamic data
Sending an application level message to MCData clients
explanation: The feature 'Accessing a list of deferred data communications' enables the MCData service to temporarily store data communications for the case where the download of the data has been deferred by an MCData user.

question: What does LACP stand for? [IEEE 802.3]
explanation: LACP stands for Link Aggregation Control Protocol and is used for the exchange of configuration information in Link Aggregation.

question: What are the enhancements specified for the 3GPP Northbound APIs in Release 16? [3GPP Release 16]
options: HTTP-based protocol or OpenAPI file improvements
explanation: The enhancements specified for the 3GPP Northbound APIs in Release 16 include optimization of APIs, handling communication failure cases, and HTTP-based protocol or OpenAPI file improvements.

question: When is the New Mode FEC field overridden in a mode switch PPDU? [IEEE 802.15.4]
options: When the New Mode FEC field has a value of zero
When the New Mode FEC field has a value of one
When the new mode packet has an SFD
When the new mode packet does not have FEC
When the Mode Switch field is set to zero

question: Which authentication method is based on WEP and requires both stations to implement WEP? [IEEE 802.11]
explanation: Shared-Key Authentication is based on WEP and requires that both stations implement WEP. It is one of the major approaches specified by 802.11 for station authentication.

question: What do the TYPE(TAG) and VLAN TPID fields in an IEEE802.1Q tagged frame specify? [IEEE 802.3]
options: The priority code of the frame
explanation: The TYPE(TAG) and VLAN TPID fields in an IEEE802.1Q tagged frame specify the VLAN identification.

question: What does OID stand for? [TCP/IP]
explanation: OID stands for Object Identifying Description.

question: Where is the UE Radio Capability ID signaled by the UE? [3GPP Release 16]
options: Over Uu interface between the UE and the CN
Within the RAN in handover procedures
explanation: The UE Radio Capability ID is signaled by the UE over Uu interface, within the RAN in handover procedures, and within the CN.

question: What is one of the requirements for interworking between fixed access and Evolved Packet Core? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Policy management and authentication for WLAN terminals
Routing different PDN connections through different accesses
Support for simultaneous access to PLMN services
Support for offline charging for traffic routed via the Evolved Packet Core
explanation: The Evolved Packet System shall be able to route different simultaneously active PDN connections through different accesses while interworking between the fixed access and Evolved Packet Core.

question: How is the modulation order (Qm) and target code rate (R) determined for PSSCH transmission? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Based on the number of REs in the slot
Based on the number of DMRS port
explanation: The UE uses the MCS table and the Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS) field in SCI format 1-A to determine the modulation order (Qm) and target code rate (R) for PSSCH transmission.

question: What are the desired characteristics for a single RedCap (reduced capability) device type?
options: Low power consumption and long battery lifetime
High data rate and low latency
Support for wearables and industrial wireless sensors
Reduced market fragmentation and economies of scale
explanation: It is desirable to support all the three use cases with a single RedCap device type to reduce market fragmentation and maximize the benefits of economies of scale.

question: What is a characteristic of SCMA (sparse code multiple access) codebook design that limits its application in large-scale systems?
explanation: The lack of scalability in SCMA codebook design limits its application in large-scale systems.

question: Which protocol is used for the exchange of configuration information between systems in Link Aggregation? [IEEE 802.3]
explanation: The IEEE 802.3ad standard describes the use of the LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) for easy exchange of configuration information between the various systems.

question: What inputs are required for the Nmfaf_3daDataManagement_Configure service operation? [3GPP Release 18]
options: Data Consumer or Analytics Consumer Information
Formatting Instructions, Processing Instructions, MFAF Notification Information, Transaction Reference Id, ADRF ID
explanation: Data Consumer or Analytics Consumer Information is required as an input for the Nmfaf_3daDataManagement_Configure service operation.

question: What is the definition of Edge Computing according to the Linux Foundation?
options: The distribution of computing capabilities to the logical extremes of a network
The use of distributed client-server systems for data storage and access
The process of analyzing and transforming data elements at the edge
The delivery of computing capabilities within the own administrative domain
The process of moving storage and computation capabilities closer to data sources
explanation: According to the Linux Foundation, Edge Computing is the distribution of computing capabilities to the logical extremes of a network.

question: What are the enhanced RRM requirements in DRX in connected mode? [3GPP Release 14]
options: Reduced cell identification delay and measurement period.
Reduced cell detection delay, measurement period, and evaluation time.
Reduced cell identification delay, measurement period, and evaluation time.
Reduced cell detection delay and measurement period.
explanation: The enhanced RRM requirements in DRX in connected mode include reducing the cell identification delay and measurement period.

question: Which TS specification defines the Proximity-based Services (ProSe) architecture? [3GPP Release 14]
explanation: The common functional architecture to support mission critical services utilizes the Proximity-based Services (ProSe) architecture defined in TS 23.303.

question: Which parameter in SL-TxProfileList-r17 indicates compatibility with DRX? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The parameter drx-Compatible in SL-TxProfileList-r17 indicates compatibility with DRX.

question: In the context of pathloss models, what is O2I? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: O2I stands for Outdoor to Indoor in the context of pathloss models.

question: What is true about services not mentioned within the interaction clause? [3GPP Release 17]
options: They have no impact on other supplementary services
They are mandatory for IMS Multimedia Telephony service
They are optional for IMS Multimedia Telephony service
They are applicable to UE accessing IMS via 3GPP accesses
They are applicable to CEPT members

question: What does O-RAN define functional blocks that are used in CF (Cell-free) mMIMO (massive multiple-input-multiple-output) networks?
explanation: O-RAN defines functional blocks having the same names precoding and combining, which are used to describe the multi-antenna processing in CF mMIMO networks.

question: What is the purpose of the Hop Dwell Time field in the Hopping Timing IE Content field? [IEEE 802.15.4]
options: To indicate the amount of time that has passed since the transmitting device hopped to the present channel.
To indicate the time interval between consecutive hops.
To indicate the number of channels hopped by the device.
To indicate the time interval for a single hop.

question: Which approach provisions a per-use-case NSI (network slice instance)?
explanation: The Use-case Specific Network Slicing approach provisions a per-use-case NSI, where the number of the NSIs equals the number of use cases.

question: What happens if two or more stations send a data frame at the same time in CSMA/CD? [IEEE 802.3]
options: The sender continues sending the frame
The receiver sends an error frame
explanation: If two or more stations send a data frame at the same time in CSMA/CD, a collision occurs.

question: What does the 5G system need to support for a UE accessing multiple network slices? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Access to the most suitable network slice in minimum time
explanation: For a UE authorized to access multiple network slices, the 5G system needs to support accessing the most suitable network slice in minimum time, minimize power consumption, and minimize service interruption time.

question: What are virtualisation-dependent items? [ETSI NFV Release 5]
options: Items whose value depends on NFV management functions
Items whose value depends on NFV infrastructure decisions
Items whose value depends on both NFV infrastructure and management functions
Items whose value depends on OSS/BSS
explanation: Virtualisation-dependent items are those items whose value is dependent on decisions made by the NFV infrastructure and/or the NFV management and orchestration functions.

question: What QoS characteristics does the MPS system support? [3GPP Release 18]
options: Specific QoS characteristics for MPS Voice, Video, and Data
Equal QoS characteristics for all MPS sessions
No QoS characteristics for MPS sessions
Priority QoS characteristics for MPS sessions
Higher QoS characteristics for MPS Voice than Video or Data
explanation: The MPS system supports the selection, enforcement, and maintenance of specific QoS characteristics for MPS Voice, Video, and Data sessions.

question: What are the key functionalities supported by the common services core in MC services? [3GPP Release 14]
explanation: The common services core supports group management, user authentication, and service configurations.

question: What is the function of the MAC sublayer in Ethernet? [IEEE 802.3]
options: Sending and receiving serial bit streams
explanation: The MAC sublayer in Ethernet is responsible for accessing the network using the CSMA/CD access mechanism and detecting collisions.

question: What does the 5G system prevent in terms of privacy for UEs using 5G LAN-type service? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The 5G system prevents the sharing of a UE's identifying information, such as SUPI and MSISDN, on private communication among UEs using 5G LAN-type service.

question: Which 3GPP specification specifies the architecture for enabling Edge Applications in 5GS? [3GPP Release 18]
explanation: TS 23.558 specifies the architecture for enabling Edge Applications in 5GS.

question: What is associated with a time and/or date setting in the IMS Multimedia Telephony service? [3GPP Release 17]
options: Activation, deactivation, and invocation of services
explanation: The activation, deactivation, and invocation of services can be associated with a time and/or date setting in the IMS Multimedia Telephony service.

question: What is the most sensitive region of the heart for inducing ventricular fibrillation (VF)? [IEEE C95.1]
explanation: The cardiac DRL applies to the apex of the heart, which has been shown to be the most sensitive region of the heart for inducing VF.

question: What is the purpose of the EAS discovery in the application layer architecture? [3GPP Release 18]
options: To provide mechanisms for an EEC to discover available EASs
To provide relevant configuration information of the EASs to the EEC
To support exposure of 3GPP network's capabilities to the EASs
To support exposure of EES's capabilities to the EASs
To support exposure of EAS's capabilities to the other EASs

question: Which entities can consume Management Data Analytics Service (MDAS)? [3GPP Release 17]
options: MnFs, NFs, SON functions, SLS assurance functions, human operators, and AFs
MnS producers, NWDAF, network and service optimization tools/functions, and AFs
Producers and consumers of network and service management
MnFs, NFs, SON functions, and AFs
explanation: Various consumers, including MnFs, NFs, SON functions, SLS assurance functions, human operators, and AFs, can consume MDAS.

question: What is the purpose of the three-way handshake in TCP? [TCP/IP]
options: To acknowledge the receipt of data
explanation: The three-way handshake is used to establish a reliable connection between two hosts or participants.

question: What is the purpose of the Authentication Algorithm Number field? [IEEE 802.11]
options: To track progress through the authentication exchange
To announce the existence of an 802.11 network at regular intervals
To identify the type of authentication used in the authentication process
To indicate the MAC address of the access point with which mobile stations are associated

question: Which solutions in LTE support configurable reliability and latency combinations? [3GPP Release 18]
options: Semi-static CFI configuration and PDSCH repetition
UL SPS repetition and PDCP packet duplication
Granular time reference provision and PDCP packet duplication
PDSCH repetition and Granular time reference provision
explanation: Semi-static CFI configuration and PDSCH repetition in LTE support configurable reliability and latency combinations.

question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for addressing and finding a route to avoid congestion within the network? [IEEE 802.3]
explanation: The Network Layer of the OSI model is responsible for addressing, finding a route, and avoiding congestion within the network.

question: What type of frames does the Ethernet transport service need to support? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The Ethernet transport service needs to support the transport of Ethernet frames.

question: What is the typical connection density in factory automation applications? [3GPP Release 17]
explanation: The typical connection density in factory automation applications is 10 connections per km2.

question: Which mitigation approaches are mentioned for network services management under migration? [ETSI NFV Release 5]
options: Transferring management requests to another NFV-MANO system
Duplicate NFV-MANO system in active-standby mode
explanation: The possible mitigation approaches mentioned are transferring management requests, duplicating NFV-MANO system, and implementing redundancy units.

question: What is the purpose of the Common API Framework (CAPIF) for 3GPP Northbound APIs? [3GPP Release 16]
options: To define a standard API framework for 3rd party Application Servers
To specify the xMB API for MBMS
To support the implementation of SEAL services
explanation: The purpose of the Common API Framework (CAPIF) for 3GPP Northbound APIs is to define a standard API framework for 3rd party Application Servers.

question: How are capability parameters signalled in the corresponding FSs for intra-band contiguous CA? [3GPP Release 18]
options: Per block of contiguous serving cells
explanation: Capability parameters for intra-band contiguous CA are signalled in the corresponding FSs per block of contiguous serving cells.

question: What does the Challenge Text in the third frame of a shared-key authentication exchange contain? [IEEE 802.11]
options: 128 bytes generated using the WEP keystream generator
A random key and initialization vector
Information elements to identify the authentication algorithm and sequence number
Status code indicating the success or failure of the authentication
explanation: The Challenge Text in the third frame of a shared-key authentication exchange contains 128 bytes generated using the WEP keystream generator.

question: According to IEEE Std 802.11-2020, when would GLK STAs find PS mode useful? [IEEE 802.11]
options: When carrying unknown traffic loads on behalf of other endpoints
When participating in the same BSS as another GLK STA
When receiving frames with the value of its TA field equal to the MAC address of another GLK STA
When transmitting Block Ack frames in an IBSS or PBSS
explanation: It is suggested that a GLK STA using a general link that carries unknown traffic loads on behalf of other endpoints not use PS mode, due to the increased delay and jitter it would cause. However, GLK STAs that find PS mode useful may utilize PS mode while performing GLK STA behaviors.

question: What is the disadvantage of address filtering in wireless networks? [IEEE 802.11]
options: It requires both stations to implement WEP
It does not synchronize timing information
It can easily be overridden by an attacker
It is a complex and lengthy process
It does not provide mutual authentication
explanation: While address filtering is better than nothing, it can easily be overridden by an attacker wishing to gain network access. MAC addresses are generally software- or firmware-programmable and can be easily changed.

question: What is the purpose of the Enhanced TNL Address Discovery with the X2 GW? [3GPP Release 17]
options: To register (H)eNBs with the X2 GW
To enhance the TNL address discovery procedure
explanation: The Enhanced TNL Address Discovery is used to enhance the TNL address discovery procedure with the X2 GW.

question: What is the scope of VNF configuration? [ETSI NFV Release 5]

question: When is the FB Tx Type subfield set to 0? [IEEE 802.11]

When the unsolicited MFB is estimated from a VHT PPDU with the RXVECTOR parameter BEAMFORMED equal to 1
explanation: The FB Tx Type subfield is set to 0 when the unsolicited MFB is estimated from a VHT PPDU with the RXVECTOR parameter BEAMFORMED equal to 0.

question: What is the purpose of providing secure means for communication scheduling information to an NPN in a 5G network? [3GPP Release 17]
options: To perform network energy saving and network resource optimization
To assign a UE to a network slice used for the third-party
To expose broadcasting capabilities to trusted third-party broadcasters' management systems
To allow a third-party to manage this trusted third-party owned application(s) in the operator's Service Hosting Environment
To monitor the resource utilization of the network service that are associated with the third-party

question: What are the ThreshServingOffloadWLAN parameters used for? [3GPP Release 17]

To define the RSRP threshold for traffic steering from WLAN to E-UTRAN.
To specify the WLAN RSSI threshold in dB.
To determine the timer value for traffic steering between E-UTRAN and WLAN.
To define the RSRP threshold for traffic steering from E-UTRAN to WLAN.

question: What is the maximum transmission power for indoor use only in Canada?

question: For FR2-2 measurement system, what is the minimum channel bandwidth required for modelling multi-path fading in single carrier scenarios? [3GPP Release 18]
explanation: For FR2-2 measurement system, a channel bandwidth of at least 400 MHz is required for modelling multi-path fading in single carrier scenarios.

question: What does 5GS act as when integrated with IEEE TSN network? [3GPP Release 18]

question: Which protocol is used for calculating the tree structure in Spanning Tree Protocol (STP)? [IEEE 802.3]

question: What is the scrambling sequence generator initialized with for a PDCCH with the CRC scrambled by G-RNTI in a common search space? [3GPP Release 17]

question: According to IEEE Std 802.11-2020, what frames should a STA transmit to indicate its intent to change power management modes? [IEEE 802.11]

question: Which RRC state is the UE in when no RRC connection is established? [3GPP Release 17]

question: What are the management aspects addressed by the OAM_LTE_WLAN work item? [3GPP Release 16]

question: How are the antenna elements placed on each antenna panel? [3GPP Release 17]

explanation: The document states that the antenna elements are placed in both the vertical and horizontal directions.

question: What is the purpose of DNS? [TCP/IP]

To filter multicast messages in Layer 2-based networks
To improve network traffic predictability and reliability
explanation: DNS provides a solution to the problem of establishing a link between host names and IP addresses by translating host names to IP addresses and vice versa.

question: What is the purpose of the map-based hybrid channel model? [3GPP Release 18]
options: To calibrate the channel model for different companies
To evaluate system performance using a digital map
To generate large-scale parameters for random clusters
To calculate angular spreads for each cluster

question: How many data pins does the MAU for twisted pair have? [IEEE 802.3]

question: What types of services can be included in a subscription? [3GPP Release 18]

Teleservices, Bearer services, and Value added services
PS CN service profile and QoS parameter ranges
Network operator services and value added services
Access services and radio access systems

question: What is the purpose of network slicing for verticals with multiple use cases?

To simplify the operations for the tenant
To improve the tenant's quality of experience

question: What is the purpose of an auto-polarity circuit in a Powered Device (PD) in a PoE system? [IEEE 802.3]
